chapters.title: The structural flaw: smart editor, dumb execution layer
Why the terminal became the center of gravity
Validation and execution: code review and coding agents
Guardrails, bounded autonomy and self-healing agents
Tool integration with MCP, reasoning and latency
Metrics, feedback loops, new roles and failure modes

takeaways: The agentic developer stack has four connected layers: orchestration in Copilot CLI, transformation by modernization agents, validation by code review agents and execution by cloud coding agents.
Agent output quality depends more on context, tools and guardrails than on the model, so maintain living project memory such as architecture files, gotchas and ADRs.
Measure throughput, quality, cycle time, developer satisfaction and technical debt, and keep humans responsible for policy, review and final decisions.
hook: AI made the editor smarter, but the real bottlenecks sit in the terminal, the pipeline and the review queue. This episode shows developers and engineering leaders how Copilot CLI, modernization, code review and coding agents form an agentic developer stack, and which context, guardrails and metrics make it work without creating new technical debt.
